data.description:
## Context / Problem

The security gate cannot run on a worker that does not already carry the scanner binaries. `RealSemgrepScanner` and `RealTrivyScanner` in `adapters/real/security_scanner.py` shell out to bare `semgrep` and `trivy`, so on the activity worker image, which ships neither, the gate raises `FileNotFoundError` from the subprocess layer rather than reporting a scanner problem.

Running the gate against `archive-massgov-pfml` also exposed a second defect. The semgrep adapter passed `--error=false`, and `semgrep --error` takes no argument, so that adapter had never produced a successful scan.

## Approach

Run each scanner from its own published image in a pod, reusing the pod transport the checks already use, and keep the existing subprocess path available for workers that do carry the binaries.

This fits because the scanners are ordinary container images that the vendors publish, so pinning an image is cheaper and more reproducible than baking two toolchains into the worker image and keeping them updated. Reusing `gates/pod_runner.py` also means the gate inherits the pod lifecycle the checks path already proved out, rather than adding a second execution mechanism.

Because the scanner runs inside a pod, the paths it reports are pod paths. The findings are remapped back to repository-relative paths before the gate sees them, so the change is invisible to every consumer of `ScanFinding`.

A missing binary now raises `ScannerError` rather than `FileNotFoundError`, so the gate reports a scanner failure instead of an unhandled exception.

## Scope

- `scripts/config.py` gains `scanner_execution`, `semgrep_image`, and `trivy_image`.
- `services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py` is new and holds `PodCommandRunner`, `pod_command_runner`, `scanner_pod_name`, `remap_paths`, `restore_paths`, and `scan_script`.
- `services/orchestration/gates/builtin.py` gains `_scanner_backend` to select subprocess or pod execution.
- `adapters/real/security_scanner.py` raises `ScannerError` when the binary is absent and drops the invalid `--error=false` argument.
- `docs/gate-engine.md` documents running the scanners from their own images.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_scanner_pod.py` is new.

## Grounded assumptions

- The scanners are invoked through a `CommandRunner` seam in `adapters/real/security_scanner.py`, so a pod-backed runner can be substituted without touching the finding parsers.
- `gates/pod_runner.py` already creates and tears down pods for the checks path, so the scanner path reuses it rather than adding new lifecycle code.
- Buildah short-name resolution covers only official Docker Hub images, so a third-party organisation image must be written as `docker.io/<org>/<image>` or it fails with "short-name resolution enforced but cannot prompt without a TTY".
- `kubectl exec` without `-t` keeps stdout and stderr on separate streams, which is what allows `scan_script` to return parseable JSON on stdout.

## Testing

Happy path: a scanner runs in a pod, emits JSON on stdout, and the findings come back with repository-relative paths. Asserted by `tests/unit/test_scanner_pod.py`.

Failure and edge paths: a missing binary on the subprocess path raises `ScannerError` rather than `FileNotFoundError`. Two scans running at once do not collide on a pod name. A finding whose location text contains the workspace prefix has only its location fields rewritten, not arbitrary body text. The scanner writes its output outside the tree it scans, so it never reports findings against its own output file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `scanner_execution` set to pod, a scan runs without either binary present on the worker, verified by a live gate run against `archive-massgov-pfml` that returns findings rather than raising.
- [ ] Reported finding paths are repository-relative, verified by `tests/unit/test_scanner_pod.py` asserting the pod workspace prefix is stripped.
- [ ] Two concurrent semgrep scans use distinct pod names, verified by a unit test asserting two calls to `scanner_pod_name` differ.
- [ ] A missing binary raises `ScannerError`, verified by a unit test.
- [ ] `semgrep` is invoked without `--error=false`, verified by `grep -rn "error=false" adapters/` returning nothing.
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
data.title: ADEVX-100: Run the built-in security scanners from their own images
